newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corp bond players tap the new issue arena.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corp bond players tap the new issue arena.

text.p: A drop in U.S. Treasury yields continues to lure corporate debt issuers into the new issue arena as financing rates become more attractive, dealers said.
"Issues are just flowing into the market," one syndicate source said. "The market is very favorable right now."
So far on Thursday, Morgan Guaranty priced $300 million in AA1/AAA two-year notes. The notes priced at par to yield 6.00 percent via JP Morgan Securities.
Meanwhile, a number of other issuers are lining up to come to market, syndicate sources said.
Coca-Cola Enterprises is expected to price $250 million in 40-year A3/AA-minus rated bonds via Salomon Brothers. The issue carries a put option in the seventh year.
Price talk on the 40-year issue is seen in the 22 t0 23 basis points area, sources said.
Medpartners is also expected to issue between $300 and $400 million in Baa3/BBB rated senior notes due 2006 via Smith Barney. Price talk is in the 95 basis points arena, dealers said.

In new secondary issues, Airtouch Communications' 7.00 percent paper was trading at a spread of 54 to 53 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, traders said. The deal priced to yield a spread of 54 basis points on Wednesnday.
Union Pacific Resources is expected to price $400 million in A3/A-rated two-part debt consisting of $200 million in 10-year debt and $200 million of 30-year debt.
Allegiance Healthcare is expected to tap the market with $500 million in a three-part debt offering via Goldman Sachs.
Among foreign issuers expected to come nearterm are Petronas with $1.0 billion in a two-part debt offering. The deal consist of $500 million each in five and 10-year debt, dealers said.
Banco Nationale de Paris is also seen tapping the market with $350 million in 10-year subordinated yankee debt out of Salomon Brothers, in early October.
Banco Santander is expected to price $150 million in 10-year subordinated yankee notes.
Brazil also is expected to tap the market with a five-year or 10-year global issue, sources said.
Dealers expect debt issuance to continue at a steady pace on Thursday, ahead of the highly anticipated release of U.S. employment numbers on Friday.
In a Reuter poll, U.S. economist predict an increase of 166,000 in September payrolls and expect the unemployment rate to rise slightly to a rate of 5.2 percent.
In the government market, the U.S. Treasury 30-year bond is off 1/32 at 98-26/32 to yield 6.84 percent.
